title: Veltrix Motors unveils Tarang mid-size SUV, bookings open ahead of October deliveries
body: Veltrix Motors on Monday unveiled the Tarang, a five- and seven-seat mid-size SUV that slots above its best-selling compact crossover. Bookings open this week at 1,200 dealerships, with deliveries begin in the second week of October. The new SUV will be offered in petrol, diesel and a 48V mild-hybrid variant, riding on 17-inch and 18-inch alloy wheels. Introductory ex-showroom prices start at INR 13.4 lakh. The company plans to build 7,000 units a month at its Chakan facility once production stabilises. "The Tarang is the most important launch in our history, and we have localised more than 92 percent of its components," said Meera Deshpande, Head of Vehicle Platform at Veltrix. Analysts expect the model to add roughly 60,000 units to Veltrix's annual volumes in FY27.

title: Veltrix Motors to invest INR 4,500 crore in new plant, lifting capacity to 6 lakh units
body: Veltrix Motors will set up a greenfield manufacturing facility at Talegaon near Pune with an investment of INR 4,500 crore, taking its total capacity to 6 lakh units per annum by FY28. The new plant will house a press shop, body shop, paint shop and two flexible assembly lines capable of building internal-combustion, hybrid and electric SUVs on the same line. Construction starts in November, with SOP targeted for Q2 2027. "This expansion is driven by a two-year order backlog on our SUV range," said Anand Kulkarni, VP Procurement, adding that supplier nominations for tyres, wheels and glass will be finalised by March 2027 with a preference for suppliers within 250 km of the site.

title: Veltrix details VX-E dedicated EV platform, three electric SUVs planned by 2028
body: Veltrix Motors has revealed VX-E, a dedicated EV platform built around a flat skateboard floor that can accommodate battery packs from 45 kWh to 79 kWh. The company plans three electric SUV models on the architecture between 2027 and 2028, the first with a claimed range of 480 km. VX-E supports front-, rear- and all-wheel drive layouts and wheel sizes from 17 to 20 inches. Meera Deshpande, Head of Vehicle Platform, said the engineering team was benchmarking low rolling resistance tyres and acoustic foam inserts to meet range and cabin-noise targets. Prototype validation runs will take place in Leh and Rajasthan this winter, and Veltrix expects to finalise its EV-specific component suppliers by the end of the year.

title: Suryan Autoworks to launch Aria compact sedan in November, targets fleet and private buyers
body: Suryan Autoworks will launch the Aria, an all-new compact sedan, on November 18, with bookings open from October 20 across its 640 outlets. The new model replaces the ageing Suryan Cruz and will come in petrol and factory-fitted CNG variant options aimed at taxi fleets. Suryan expects the Aria to sell 5,500 units a month in its first year, with roughly a third going to fleet customers. Karthik Raghavan, Chief Purchasing Officer, said the sedan uses 15-inch wheels across trims and that component sourcing was completed locally in Tamil Nadu. Pricing is expected to start near INR 7.2 lakh ex-showroom, undercutting key rivals.

title: Suryan Autoworks announces brownfield expansion at Oragadam, adds 1.5 lakh units of capacity
body: Suryan Autoworks will add a second assembly line at its Oragadam plant in a INR 1,800 crore brownfield expansion, raising installed capacity to 4.2 lakh units per annum. The new production line will build the upcoming Aria sedan and a compact SUV due in 2027. Work has begun and trial production is scheduled for Q1 2027. "Demand from fleet operators has been running ahead of our capacity for three quarters," said Karthik Raghavan, Chief Purchasing Officer, who confirmed that the company will run fresh sourcing rounds for high-volume components, including tyres and wheel assemblies, to support the ramp-up.

title: Kavero Electric unveils K7 electric SUV on second-generation EV architecture
body: Kavero Electric today unveiled the K7, a battery electric SUV built on the second generation of its in-house EV architecture. The K7 offers a 72 kWh pack with a certified range of 520 km and 150 kW DC fast charging. Bookings open in December and customer deliveries begin in March 2027 from the company's Hosakote plant. Nikhil Rao, CTO, said the SUV was developed with 19-inch low-drag wheels and required tyres with low rolling resistance and reduced road noise, given the absence of engine sound masking. Kavero targets 3,000 units a month of the K7 at peak, making it the company's highest-volume launch to date.

title: Kavero Electric picks Dharwad for greenfield EV plant with 2.5 lakh units capacity
body: Kavero Electric has selected Dharwad in north Karnataka for its second vehicle manufacturing facility, a greenfield project that will add 2.5 lakh units per annum of capacity by 2028. The company will invest INR 6,200 crore in the new plant, which will include a battery pack assembly line, general assembly and an end-of-line test track. Divya Shenoy, Head of Supplier Development, said Kavero will set up a supplier park adjacent to the site and invite tier-1 partners for tyres, seating and wiring harnesses to co-locate. The first phase of the expansion is due to start production in Q3 2027.

title: Zentro EV launches Z1 electric hatchback at INR 8.9 lakh, eyes fleet buyers
body: Hyderabad startup Zentro EV has launched the Z1, a compact battery electric hatchback with a 30 kWh pack and a claimed range of 310 km. The car is priced at INR 8.9 lakh ex-showroom, and bookings open immediately in 12 cities, with deliveries begin in January. A fleet variant with a heavy-duty suspension and extended warranty is aimed at cab aggregators. "Our unit economics depend on keeping energy consumption low, and that means every component, down to the tyres, has to be optimised for efficiency," said Aditya Reddy, co-founder and CEO. Zentro plans to produce 25,000 units in its first full year.

title: Arohan Two Wheelers launches Stride 125 commuter motorcycle, targets 40,000 units a month
body: Arohan Two Wheelers has launched the Stride 125, a new model in the fast-growing 125cc commuter segment. The motorcycle features a single-channel ABS variant, tubeless tyres on 17-inch alloy wheels and a claimed fuel efficiency of 65 km per litre. Ex-showroom prices start at INR 89,500 and deliveries begin next week. Priya Iyer, Head of Product Planning, said the Stride 125 will also be exported to 18 countries in Africa and Latin America from early 2027. Arohan expects monthly volumes of 40,000 units once the Hosur line ramps up, making it one of the brand's three highest-volume models.

title: Arohan Two Wheelers to expand Hosur capacity by 1 million units with new assembly line
body: Arohan Two Wheelers will invest INR 950 crore to add a fourth assembly line at Hosur, taking total capacity to 4.8 million units per annum. The expansion responds to strong rural demand and export growth, the company said. The new production line, due to be commissioned by June 2027, will be able to build both petrol and electric scooters. Senthil Kumar, VP Materials & Procurement, said Arohan would double the number of approved tyre sources for scooter and motorcycle fitment to de-risk supply as volumes climb.

title: Pulsewing Mobility reveals new EV platform for five electric scooter models
body: Pulsewing Mobility has revealed Pulse Core, a new EV platform that will underpin five electric scooter and light motorcycle models over the next 24 months. The architecture uses a common battery electric drivetrain with packs from 2.5 kWh to 5 kWh and a range of up to 190 km. The first two models, the Pulse Air and Pulse Max, will reach showrooms in Q1 2027. Varun Hegde, Chief Product Officer, said the platform was designed around 12-inch and 14-inch wheels and that the company was evaluating low rolling resistance tyre compounds to extend range by up to 6 percent.

title: Bharatrath Commercial Vehicles commissions new plant for heavy trucks in Lucknow
body: Bharatrath Commercial Vehicles has started construction of a new plant on the outskirts of Lucknow to build heavy trucks and tippers, adding capacity of 60,000 units per annum. The INR 2,300 crore greenfield facility is expected to begin production in Q4 2027 and will include a cab-weld shop and a dedicated axle assembly line. Rajesh Tiwari, VP Procurement, said the company is shortlisting radial tyre suppliers for 10-, 12- and 16-wheeler configurations as part of the expansion, and expects mining and infrastructure tippers to account for 35 percent of output.

title: Bharatrath unveils 55-tonne tractor-trailer and new tipper range at expo
body: Bharatrath Commercial Vehicles unveiled a 55-tonne tractor-trailer and a refreshed range of 28- and 35-tonne tippers at a trade expo in Greater Noida. The new model line-up features a more fuel-efficient 7.2-litre engine and tubeless radial tyres as standard across all variants. Sanjay Mishra, Head of Truck Platforms, said the tractor-trailer was designed for long-haul container movement on the new expressways and that bookings open at dealerships next month. Commercial deliveries begin in January, with Bharatrath targeting 1,500 units a month across the range.

title: Stallion Bus & Coach bags order for 1,200 buses from three state transport corporations
body: Stallion Bus & Coach has secured an order for 1,200 diesel and CNG buses from state transport corporations in Karnataka, Maharashtra and Goa, its largest single win to date. The buses, a mix of 12-metre intercity coaches and 10-metre city buses, will be built at the company's Dharwad works, with units to be delivered in batches between December and August 2027. Ganesh Patil, Director – Supply Chain, said the company would procure radial tyres, seats and HVAC units for the full order by November. The contract is valued at about INR 540 crore.

title: Greenline eBus wins 2,400 e-buses under central government scheme for nine cities
body: Greenline eBus has been declared the lowest bidder for 2,400 electric buses under the central government's e-bus scheme, which funds operators on a per-kilometre subsidy for 12 years. The ministry notified the award last week, covering nine cities including Hyderabad, Pune and Surat. The buses will be supplied and operated on a gross-cost contract, with the first 600 units to be delivered by June 2027. Srinivas Rao, CEO, said Greenline would procure components for the order locally and was scaling its Hyderabad line to 250 buses a month. Kavya Menon, VP Procurement, confirmed that tyre supply for the fleet will be contracted on a cost-per-km basis.

title: Cabzy Mobility to deploy 10,000 electric cabs in fleet electrification push
body: Ride-hailing platform Cabzy Mobility will deploy 10,000 electric cabs across Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Delhi and Mumbai over the next 18 months, electrifying nearly 40 percent of its owned fleet. The company has placed an order with two domestic EV makers for sedans and hatchbacks, and will lease the vehicles to driver-partners on a weekly plan. "Fleet electrification lowers our cost per km, but only if tyre and brake wear are controlled — EVs are heavier and more torque-heavy," said Arjun Malhotra, Fleet Operations Head. Cabzy expects the first 2,000 e-cabs on the road by March 2027.

title: Cabzy Mobility announces fleet expansion into eight tier-2 cities
body: Cabzy Mobility will extend its owned fleet into eight tier-2 cities, including Coimbatore, Indore and Lucknow, adding 3,500 cars by the end of the fiscal year. The fleet expansion will be led by CNG sedans in the near term, with electric models added as charging infrastructure matures. Neha Kapoor, Chief Operating Officer, said the company would procure vehicles and consumables centrally and was renegotiating maintenance contracts to cover the larger footprint. Cabzy plans to open service hubs in each city to handle tyre rotation, alignment and preventive maintenance in-house.

title: RouteMile Logistics places an order for 1,500 trucks to expand its long-haul fleet
body: RouteMile Logistics has placed an order for 1,500 heavy trucks, including 1,100 tractor-trailers and 400 multi-axle rigid trucks, in its biggest fleet expansion to date. The vehicles will be sourced from two domestic truck makers, with units to be delivered over the next 10 months. Vikram Choudhary, Head of Fleet & Maintenance, said RouteMile is moving its entire fleet to a cost-per-km tyre programme with retreading and wanted a single partner for new and replacement tyres. The company operates about 7,800 trucks today on routes connecting the NCR, Gujarat and the east coast ports.

title: SwiftKart Fleet Services to procure 5,000 cargo three-wheelers for last-mile fleet
body: SwiftKart Fleet Services will procure 5,000 electric cargo three-wheelers and 800 small vans over the next year, more than doubling its last-mile fleet in Mumbai, Pune and Ahmedabad. The company has placed an order for the first 2,000 units with Trimurti Auto, with units to be delivered from November. Imran Shaikh, Fleet Operations Head, said the vehicles would run around 120 km a day on dense urban routes and that SwiftKart was evaluating puncture-resistant tyre options to cut downtime. SwiftKart deploys vehicles for several large e-commerce and quick-commerce platforms.

title: Kronhaus Automobil commits EUR 400 million investment in India, plans new plant near Chennai
body: German premium carmaker Kronhaus Automobil will make an investment in India of EUR 400 million over five years, including a new plant near Chennai to assemble two SUVs and an electric crossover. The facility will have an initial capacity of 40,000 units per annum. Matthias Weber, Head of Purchasing – Asia, said Kronhaus aims for 70 percent localisation by 2029 and will run local sourcing events for tyres, glass and interior trim in early 2027. Rahul Menon, Managing Director of Kronhaus India, said the move would cut landed prices by up to 18 percent and make the brand competitive in the luxury SUV segment.

title: Hoshida Motor to invest INR 5,000 crore in India operations over three years
body: Hoshida Motor Corporation will invest INR 5,000 crore in its India operations over three years, the Japanese carmaker said, as it prepares two new hybrid SUVs and a compact MPV for the market. The investment covers tooling, a new engine line and a supplier development programme to deepen localisation from 78 percent to 90 percent. Kenji Takahashi, President of Hoshida Motor India, said the country will become an export hub for Africa and the Middle East. Suresh Pillai, Director – Localisation, said the company would qualify additional Indian tyre suppliers for original fitment.

title: Daeyang Motors confirms India market entry with wholly owned subsidiary and Anantapur plant
body: South Korea's Daeyang Motors has confirmed its India market entry through a wholly owned subsidiary and a manufacturing facility at Anantapur in Andhra Pradesh. The company will invest USD 900 million in the first phase, which includes a plant with capacity of 1.8 lakh units per annum. Park Ji-hoon, Head of India Programme, said the first model would be a mid-size SUV launching in late 2027, followed by an MPV. Harish Nair, Director – Supplier Quality, said Daeyang would audit Indian component makers from January, with tyres and wheels among the first categories for local sourcing.

title: Ampera Dynamics forms joint venture to build battery electric crossovers in India
body: US electric vehicle maker Ampera Dynamics has signed a joint venture with a Pune-based engineering group to manufacture battery electric crossovers in India from 2028. The partners will invest USD 350 million initially, and the venture will localise 60 percent of components within three years. Ananya Bhatt, Country Head – India, said the crossover would be built on Ampera's ev architecture with a range of 450 km and would also be exported to Southeast Asia. Daniel Brooks, VP Global Sourcing, said the company would begin local sourcing discussions with Indian tyre and seating suppliers this quarter.

title: Terraforge Equipment wins tender for 140 rigid dumpers for iron ore mining
body: Terraforge Equipment has won a tender to supply 140 rigid dump trucks of 60-tonne and 100-tonne class to a state-owned iron ore mining company in Odisha. The dumper order, worth about INR 1,150 crore, will be executed over 20 months from the company's Nagpur works. Prakash Deshmukh, VP Procurement, said Terraforge would contract OTR tyres for the full order upfront given long lead times for large earthmoving sizes. The company also expects follow-on tenders for wheel loaders and graders at two new quarry sites.

title: Deccan Earthmovers to set up new plant for excavators, doubling capacity
body: Deccan Earthmovers will build a new plant at Tumakuru for excavators and backhoe loaders, doubling capacity to 24,000 units per annum by 2028. The INR 1,400 crore greenfield project will include a fabrication shop, paint line and assembly line with automated testing. Manjunath Gowda, Director – Supply Chain, said the expansion is driven by highway and quarry demand, and the company would add new suppliers for OTR and industrial tyres. Production is expected to start in Q2 2027. The company has also appointed a project director to oversee land acquisition and hiring of about 1,100 workers.

title: Orbis Mining Services floats tender for 180 haul trucks and OTR tyres
body: Orbis Mining Services has floated a tender to procure 180 haul trucks and a five-year OTR tyre supply contract for its coal and iron ore mining operations in Jharkhand and Odisha. The contractor is expanding its fleet after winning mine-developer-and-operator contracts for three blocks. Abhishek Sinha, Head of Equipment & Fleet, said bidders must support on-site tyre management, pressure monitoring and repair bays at each pit. Bids are due by November 15, and trucks are to be delivered in phases from March 2027.

title: Meridian Tractors launches new 45–60 hp tractor series for north India
body: Meridian Tractors has launched the Pro Series, a new model range of 45 to 60 hp tractors aimed at paddy and sugarcane farmers in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. The range includes a 4WD variant and comes with larger rear tyres for improved traction in wet fields. Ex-showroom prices start at INR 7.6 lakh. Harleen Kaur, Head of Product Management, said deliveries begin ahead of the rabi season and the company expects the Pro Series to account for a quarter of its domestic volumes in FY27.

title: Yatrigo Rides to electrify its entire cab fleet in Delhi-NCR by 2027
body: Yatrigo Rides will convert its entire Delhi-NCR fleet of 4,200 cabs to electric cabs by the end of 2027, making it one of the largest all-EV fleet operators in the region. The company has signed agreements for 3,000 electric sedans and is setting up three charging-and-service depots. Siddharth Jain, co-founder and COO, said salaried driver-partners would be trained on regenerative braking to reduce component wear. Mohit Arora, Fleet Maintenance Manager, said Yatrigo was seeking tyre suppliers who could guarantee mileage for heavier EVs running 250 km a day.

title: Lionspeed Motorcycles launches Ridgeback 650 adventure tourer
body: Lionspeed Motorcycles has launched the Ridgeback 650, an adventure tourer powered by its parallel-twin engine, with spoked 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wheels shod with dual-purpose tyres. Priced from INR 3.49 lakh ex-showroom, the motorcycle will be sold in India and 30 export markets. Bookings open today and deliveries begin in November. Tanya Fernandes, VP Product Strategy, said the new model is expected to add 4,000 units a month and the company had already sourced a tubeless spoke-wheel variant for 2027.

title: Voltway Mobility announces USD 120 million investment in India for electric scooter plant
body: Singapore-based Voltway Mobility will make a USD 120 million investment in India to build electric scooters and motorcycles at a new facility in Hosur, marking its market entry into the country. The plant will produce 3 lakh units a year on the company's dedicated EV platform, with the first electric scooter model due in mid-2027. Wei Ling Tan, CEO, said India would become Voltway's largest market and export base. Kiran Joshi, Director – India Operations, said the company targets 80 percent localisation and will begin local sourcing of tyres, wheels and battery enclosures immediately.

title: Desertline Transport places an order for 800 heavy trucks for GCC fleet expansion
body: Dubai-based Desertline Transport has placed an order for 800 heavy trucks with Bharatrath Commercial Vehicles as part of a fleet expansion to serve port and construction logistics across the UAE, Oman and Saudi Arabia. The trucks will be delivered over 14 months. Omar Al Hashimi, Fleet Director, said the company wants tyres engineered for high ambient temperatures and long highway stints, and will procure replacement tyres through a regional fleet programme. The deal is one of the largest export orders for an Indian truck maker in the region this year.

title: Trimurti Auto gets PLI scheme approval, plans capacity expansion for e-rickshaws
body: Trimurti Auto has received approval under the government's PLI scheme for advanced automotive technology, making it eligible for incentive payouts of up to 13 percent on eligible sales for five years. The ministry notified the list of approved applicants on Friday. Alok Agarwal, Managing Director, said the company would use the incentive to fund a capacity expansion at Kanpur, adding a new production line for electric loaders and e-rickshaws that will lift output to 1.2 lakh units a year by 2027.

title: Coastal Interstate Bus Lines to add 600 buses in fleet expansion across south India
body: Coastal Interstate Bus Lines will add 600 buses, including 250 sleeper coaches, over the next 12 months, in a fleet expansion across Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana. The operator has placed an order for 400 coaches with Stallion Bus & Coach, with the remainder to be tendered in January. Thomas Kurian, Director – Fleet, said the company runs its coaches over 18,000 km a month and would procure tyres under a cost-per-km agreement with retreading support at its Kochi and Bengaluru depots.

title: Telangana EV policy incentive to back Zentro EV's second manufacturing phase
body: The Telangana government has cleared a special incentive package for Zentro EV under the state EV policy, including a capital subsidy of 25 percent on plant and machinery and a full waiver of stamp duty. The package was notified by the industries department on Tuesday. Zentro will use the support to begin the second phase of its Hyderabad plant, which will double output of the Z1 hatchback. Sneha Varma, VP Operations, said the company was also applying under the central PLI scheme and expected to lift annual production to 60,000 units by 2028.

title: Hoshida Motor launches Verano hybrid SUV in India, bookings open
body: Hoshida Motor India has launched the Verano, a new SUV with a strong-hybrid powertrain delivering a claimed 27 km per litre. The new model is built at the company's Bidadi plant and is priced from INR 16.9 lakh ex-showroom. Bookings open today and deliveries begin in the first week of November. Kenji Takahashi, President of Hoshida Motor India, said the Verano would be offered in two variant options with 17-inch and 18-inch wheels and was expected to sell 6,000 units a month.

title: Veltrix compact crossover prototype spied testing near Nashik
body: A camouflaged prototype believed to be a new compact crossover from Veltrix Motors has been spotted testing on the highway near Nashik. The test mule appears to share its front structure with the brand's current compact SUV but has a longer rear overhang and new tail lamps. Veltrix declined to comment on the car, and industry sources say the project may still be two years away from production. Dealers in Maharashtra said they had not received any communication about a new product for next year. Such early prototypes often undergo significant changes before any decision on a market debut is taken.

title: Pulsewing Mobility runs small battery-swapping pilot with 50 delivery riders
body: Pulsewing Mobility has started a three-month battery-swapping pilot with 50 delivery riders in Koramangala and HSR Layout. Riders use four swap stations installed at partner petrol pumps and can exchange a depleted pack in under two minutes. The company said the trial is exploratory and it has not decided whether to invest in a larger network. Varun Hegde, Chief Product Officer, said the pilot would help Pulsewing understand rider behaviour and pack health data. Similar pilots by other brands have been paused in the past after utilisation remained low.

title: Meridian Tractors explores export opportunities in East Africa
body: Meridian Tractors is studying export opportunities in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda, where demand for low-horsepower tractors has been rising with farm mechanisation. A company delegation visited Nairobi last month and met distributors and agricultural cooperatives. Gurpreet Singh, VP Procurement, said no decision had been taken on volumes or a local assembly partner and that the company would first evaluate homologation requirements. Analysts say it could take up to 18 months before any shipments start, if the company decides to proceed at all.

title: Lionspeed Motorcycles appoints new head of design, hints at future products
body: Lionspeed Motorcycles has appointed Marco Bellini, formerly of an Italian design studio, as its new head of design. The company said Bellini will lead styling for motorcycles planned for the second half of the decade and will be based at its Chennai technical centre. Tanya Fernandes, VP Product Strategy, said the appointment reflects Lionspeed's ambition to compete in more premium segments globally but gave no details on specific products or timelines. Bellini will also oversee a new colour and trim studio for accessories and riding gear.

title: SwiftKart trials pedal-assist cargo bikes for short deliveries in Pune
body: SwiftKart is trialling 20 pedal-assist cargo bikes for grocery deliveries within a two-kilometre radius of its dark stores in Pune. The pilot, which runs until December, will test whether bikes can replace scooters for very short trips in congested neighbourhoods. Sonal Mehta, who leads sourcing at SwiftKart, said the company would review rider feedback and delivery times before deciding whether to extend the trial to other cities. The bikes are leased from a local startup and carry insulated boxes of up to 40 kg.

title: Daeyang Motors hires consultants to study Indian dealer network
body: Daeyang Motors has hired a consulting firm to study dealer network models in India, including franchise, agency and online-first retail. People familiar with the matter said the study will take six months and cover 40 cities. Park Ji-hoon, Head of India Programme, told reporters the company was still finalising its product plan for the country and would announce details later. Industry observers say the study suggests Daeyang is thinking beyond an initial single-model strategy, though the company did not confirm any timelines.

title: Deccan Earthmovers signs MoU to set up operator skill centre in Karnataka
body: Deccan Earthmovers has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Karnataka skill development department to set up a training centre for construction equipment operators in Tumakuru. The centre will train 2,000 operators a year on backhoe loaders and compactors using simulators and a practice yard. Rekha Prasad, Senior Manager – Sourcing, said the programme would help address the shortage of skilled operators on highway projects. The company did not disclose the investment involved. The first batch of trainees is expected to enrol in April, and the course will be certified by the state's technical education board.

title: Yatrigo Rides considers intercity rides from Delhi to nearby tourist towns
body: Yatrigo Rides is considering adding intercity trips from Delhi to Agra, Jaipur and Rishikesh, according to people familiar with its plans. The company is surveying customers on pricing and whether they would prefer round-trip or one-way bookings. Siddharth Jain, co-founder and COO, said the idea was at an early stage and would depend on driver availability and toll costs. Rival platforms have seen mixed results with intercity products, which tend to be seasonal. Any rollout would likely begin with weekend-only trips from central Delhi pickup points.

title: Kronhaus Automobil reviewing Asian component sourcing amid currency swings
body: Kronhaus Automobil is reviewing where it buys components for its Asian assembly sites after currency swings raised costs in the first half. Matthias Weber, Head of Purchasing – Asia, said the carmaker was looking at greater localisation where quality standards could be met, but stressed that no supplier changes had been decided. The review covers electronics, interior parts and chassis components across Thailand, Malaysia and India. Results are expected in the spring. Some analysts believe the exercise is mainly aimed at renegotiating prices with existing vendors rather than switching sources.

title: Stallion Bus & Coach showcases concept luxury coach at Bengaluru expo
body: Stallion Bus & Coach displayed a concept luxury coach with reclining pod seats, onboard washrooms and a panoramic glass roof at a transport expo in Bengaluru. The company said the concept was designed to gauge operator interest in a premium product and that production would depend on feedback. Asha Kamath, Head of Institutional Sales, said several private operators had asked for pricing, but no commercial decision had been made. The coach is built on a 14.5-metre multi-axle chassis. The concept also features a driver-assistance camera suite and a redesigned luggage bay with 12 cubic metres of space.

title: Suryan Autoworks Q1 profit misses estimates on higher steel costs
body: Suryan Autoworks reported a 14 percent year-on-year fall in first-quarter net profit to INR 412 crore, missing analyst estimates, as higher steel and aluminium prices squeezed margins. Revenue rose 6 percent to INR 9,870 crore. EBITDA margin contracted 180 basis points to 9.1 percent. The company said it had taken a small price increase in August and expected commodity pressures to ease in the second half. Shares fell 3.2 percent in early trade on the Bombay bourse. Management reiterated its dividend guidance for the year.

title: Veltrix Motors managing director named business leader of the year
body: The managing director of Veltrix Motors has been named business leader of the year at an awards ceremony in Mumbai, recognising the company's turnaround over the past five years. The jury cited improvements in profitability, dealer satisfaction and corporate governance. Accepting the award, he credited employees and dealer partners and spoke about the importance of mentoring young engineers. The event was attended by more than 400 executives from the manufacturing and financial services sectors. Veltrix shares were little changed on the news, and the company did not issue any statement beyond thanking the organisers.

title: Driver union files lawsuit against Cabzy Mobility over commission rates
body: A drivers' union in Karnataka has filed a lawsuit against Cabzy Mobility in the state high court, alleging that the company's commission rates breach the state's aggregator guidelines. The union is seeking a cap of 15 percent on commissions and compensation for past deductions. Cabzy said it was complying with all applicable rules and would contest the case. The hearing has been listed for next month. The dispute follows protests at the company's Bengaluru offices in August. Legal experts said the outcome could set a precedent for how aggregator commissions are regulated across other states.

title: Arohan Two Wheelers signs three-year title sponsorship of regional cricket league
body: Arohan Two Wheelers has signed a three-year title sponsorship deal for a regional T20 cricket league in Tamil Nadu. The league, which features eight franchises, will be broadcast on a regional sports channel and streamed online. Financial terms were not disclosed. Priya Iyer, Head of Product Planning, said cricket remained the most effective way to reach young commuters in smaller towns. The brand will also run in-stadium activations and fan contests during the season. The deal follows a similar tie-up the brand signed last year with a kabaddi franchise in Karnataka.

title: Hoshida Motor recalls 18,000 cars in India to replace airbag sensor
body: Hoshida Motor India is recalling about 18,000 units of its compact sedan manufactured between March and June to inspect and replace a faulty airbag control sensor. The company said no injuries had been reported and owners would be contacted by dealers for a free replacement taking about an hour. The issue was traced to a batch of sensors from an overseas supplier. Hoshida said the recall was voluntary and part of its commitment to customer safety. Owners can check whether their car is affected by entering the chassis number on the company's website.

title: Kavero Electric CFO resigns to pursue other opportunities
body: Kavero Electric said its chief financial officer has resigned to pursue opportunities outside the company, effective at the end of October. The board has started a search for a successor, and the financial controller will serve as interim head of finance. Kavero said the departure was not related to any disagreement on accounting or governance matters. The company is expected to report half-yearly results in November and is reportedly preparing for a stock market listing in 2028. The outgoing CFO joined Kavero four years ago from a consumer goods company and oversaw two private funding rounds.

title: Bharatrath Commercial Vehicles declares interim dividend of INR 6 per share
body: The board of Bharatrath Commercial Vehicles has declared an interim dividend of INR 6 per share for the current fiscal year, with the record date set for October 10. The payout totals about INR 190 crore. The company also approved the reappointment of two independent directors for a second term of five years. Shares closed 1.1 percent higher on the day. Analysts said the payout reflected strong cash generation despite a cautious outlook for the sector. The company's net debt stood at INR 340 crore at the end of June, down from INR 610 crore a year earlier.

title: Lionspeed Motorcycles names film star as brand ambassador
body: Lionspeed Motorcycles has signed a popular Tamil film actor as its brand ambassador for a two-year period. The actor will feature in television commercials, social media content and riding events organised by the company's owners' club. Tanya Fernandes, VP Product Strategy, said the association would help the brand connect with younger riders in south India. The first campaign will air during the festive season. Industry watchers said celebrity endorsements remain popular among two-wheeler brands, though their impact on sales is difficult to measure. The contract value was not disclosed, but people familiar with the deal said it was among the largest in the category.

title: RouteMile Logistics reports data breach affecting customer invoices
body: RouteMile Logistics has reported a cybersecurity incident in which an unauthorised party accessed a server containing customer invoices and shipment records. The company said it had isolated the affected systems, informed the national cyber agency and engaged forensic experts. No payment card data was stored on the server. Ritu Bansal, VP Procurement, said customers would receive notifications this week. The company's shares fell 2 percent after the disclosure. RouteMile said its operations were unaffected and shipments continued as normal. The company plans to complete an external security audit by December.

title: Zentro EV in trademark dispute with appliance maker over brand name
body: Zentro EV is facing a trademark dispute after a consumer appliance maker objected to its use of the Zentro name, claiming prior registration in several classes. The appliance company has sought an injunction in the Delhi High Court. Zentro said its registration covered vehicles and related services and that it did not expect any disruption to its business. Legal experts said such disputes are often settled out of court through coexistence agreements. The next hearing in the case is scheduled for early December, and both sides have been asked to explore mediation.

title: Kavero Electric to build in-house power electronics and battery pack plant
body: Kavero Electric will invest INR 1,600 crore to bring inverter, onboard charger and battery management system production in-house at a new facility in Hosakote. The plant will assemble power modules using silicon carbide MOSFETs and will also produce battery packs for the company's electric SUV range. Nikhil Rao, CTO, said the move would cut drivetrain costs by 15 percent and reduce dependence on imported power semiconductors. Kavero is in talks with chip suppliers for long-term wafer and module supply agreements, and will hire 800 engineers for the facility.

title: Greenline eBus to build 14 solar-powered charging depots for city e-bus fleet
body: Greenline eBus will build 14 charging depots with rooftop solar and battery storage to power its growing fleet of electric buses in Hyderabad, Pune and Surat. Each depot will host up to 120 buses and 3 MW of rooftop and carport solar. Srinivas Rao, CEO, said the company would tender for solar EPC, grid connections and 40 MWh of storage by December. The depots will also include maintenance bays for tyres, brakes and HVAC servicing to keep buses on the road for 18 hours a day.

title: Veltrix Motors opens rail-linked vehicle logistics hub near Pune
body: Veltrix Motors has opened a 60-acre vehicle logistics hub with a rail siding near its Chakan plant, capable of dispatching 25,000 cars a month by rail to eastern and northern India. The hub includes covered yards, a pre-delivery inspection shed and a fleet of car-carrier trucks operated by logistics partners. Rohit Sawant, Director – Supply Chain, said moving more volumes by rail would cut outbound logistics costs by 12 percent as the company prepares for its new plant and higher capacity from 2027.

title: Cabzy Mobility builds 40 charging hubs with rooftop solar for EV fleet
body: Cabzy Mobility will build 40 fast-charging hubs with rooftop solar across four cities to support its fleet electrification plan. Each hub will have 30 DC chargers and a service bay for tyre and brake maintenance. Neha Kapoor, Chief Operating Officer, said the company was negotiating power purchase agreements for 25 MW of renewable energy to keep charging costs predictable for driver-partners. The hubs will begin opening in January, starting with Bengaluru and Hyderabad. Cabzy expects renewable power to supply more than 60 percent of its charging demand by 2028.

title: Ampera Dynamics plans India cell module and BMS electronics facility
body: Ampera Dynamics will set up a battery module and battery management system electronics facility in Pune to support its planned battery electric crossover production in India. The USD 180 million project will assemble cell modules and populate BMS circuit boards using locally sourced semiconductors where possible. Daniel Brooks, VP Global Sourcing, said the company was seeking suppliers of power semiconductors, printed circuit boards and thermal interface materials. The facility is expected to be operational by mid-2028. Ampera has shortlisted two industrial parks near Chakan and expects to employ 600 people at full operation.
